region.text: the Kalat country around Kalat in Sarawan and Jhalawan

ledger.note: 1666: Mir Ahmad Khan I founds the Khanate of Kalat. 'Formed in 1666 when Mir Ahmad Khan I declared independence from Mughal suzerainty' (infobox Established 1666; capital Kalat). The page names the Kalat country, not a boundary.

region.text: Quetta, Mastung and Pishin, taken from the Mughal governor of Kandahar

ledger.note: Mir Ahmad I (1666-1695) 'took Quetta, Mastung, and Pishin from the Mughal governor of Kandahar'. The page gives no year within his reign; 1666 is a bridging choice.
Samandar Khan (1697-1714) 'expanded to Karachi; the Mughals gave him the port'. The page gives his reign, not a year; 1697 is a bridging choice.

region.text: the coast from Karachi to Bandar Abbas

ledger.note: Abdullah Khan (1716-1731) 'extended the state to Bandar Abbas'. The page gives his reign, not a year; the coast between Karachi and Bandar Abbas is the researcher's reading (Makran).

region.text: Kacchi, the plain below the Bolan, given by Nader Shah

ledger.note: 1734: Nader Shah gives Kacchi to Mehrab Khan ('Nader Shah gave Kacchi to Mehrab Khan (1734-1749) as compensation for his father's death'). The Battle of Kachhi in which Abdullah Khan fell is 1734 on this page and 1731 on the Nasir Khan page.

region.text: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand and Zahedan in what is now Iran

ledger.counterpart: local rulers of Persian Baluchistan (page silent)
ledger.note: Nasir Khan I (1749-1794) 'conquered Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, and Zahedan'. The page gives his reign, not years; 1749 is the start of his reign (Nasir Khan page: 'Nasir Khan began his reign after Ahmad Shah Durrani replaced Haji Khan').

region.text: the Kalat country around Kalat in Sarawan and Jhalawan

ledger.note: 1758: Nasir Khan declares independence after the Marathas expel the Afghans from Punjab; Ahmad Shah Durrani besieges Kalat 'for about 40 days and failed to take it'.

region.text: the Kalat country around Kalat in Sarawan and Jhalawan

ledger.note: 1758: peace. Afghan forces besieged Kalat and 'both sides agreed to peace'; by the Treaty of Kalat Nasir Khan 'remained governor and acknowledged Ahmad Shah's overlordship', exempt from annual tribute but supplying men.

region.text: the port of Gwadar, given to Sultan bin Ahmad in 1784

ledger.note: 1784: Gwadar to Oman. Nasir Khan 'gave refuge to the Omani prince Sayyed Sultan bin Ahmad' and 'gave him only the port of Gwadar'; it became part of Oman when Sultan took the throne in 1792 and stayed Omani until Pakistan bought it in 1958 (Khanate page). [Reviewer sa-06-x, 2026-10-25: counterpart set to the slug sultanate-of-oman: the Khanate page says Nasir Khan 'gifted him the port of Gwadar' and that 'Gwadar continued to be part of Sultanate of Oman until it was purchased by Pakistan in 1958'; the sultanate-of-oman dossier records Gwadar as a gain 'by 1783'.]

union.text: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand and Zahedan in what is now Iran

region.text: Persian Baluchistan: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Zahedan and the Iranian Makran coast

ledger.note: Early 19th century: the khanate 'lost much of its territory to Qajar Iran and the Emirate of Afghanistan' (no years on the page). The Iranian half is drawn here as the Persian Baluchistan conquests of 1749 and the Iranian Makran coast, at 1828 (the year the Emirate of Afghanistan row begins) as a bridging choice; the Afghan share is not drawn because the page names no land.
13 November 1839: the British storm Kalat ('Siege of Kalat (13 November 1839)'; 'Kalat city was sacked by the British'). Shah Nawaz Khan reigns 1839-1841.
1841: the occupation ends. The page lists Shah Nawaz Khan 1839-1841 and Nasir Khan II from 1841 and says nothing about the British leaving; the year is bridged from the change of khan.

Karachi: no page opened dates the loss of the port Samandar Khan received. Karachi lies in Sindh, which the East India Company annexed from the Talpurs in 1843 (Battle of Miani and Hyderabad, 1843), so the khanate cannot have held it after 1843; 1843 is the bridging bound.

region.text: Quetta and Pishin, which became British Baluchistan

ledger.note: 1877: the Baluchistan Agency is established 'following the 1876 treaty'; its territories included areas 'acquired by lease or otherwise brought under direct British control'. The page does not name Quetta or Pishin or date any lease; Quetta and Pishin, the khanate's towns on the Bolan-Kandahar road, are the researcher's reading and 1877 the bridging year.

region.text: Kharan, a separate princely state by 1941

ledger.note: Kharan separates: 'Kharan became a separate princely state between the 1931 and 1941 censuses' (the Agency page lists Kharan State and Las Bela State with Kalat as princely states in 1941). 1941 is the first year the page shows it separate.
14 October 1955: the Khanate of Kalat ends, merged into West Pakistan. Infobox 'Disestablished 1955'; Ahmad Yar Khan (1933-1955) was the last Khan.

certainty.note: A tribal confederacy's reach across Balochistan: no page opened gives a boundary, and the 1835 infobox area is a claim.
The Iran frontier was demarcated in 1896 and is sharp from then; the internal frontiers with the Agency districts and the feudatory states stay soft.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks (no row under any Kalat name): cliopatria_names is empty and every keyframe is new. Three pages opened (Khanate of Kalat, Baluchistan Agency, Nasir Khan Noori); WebFetch returned extracts.

What the pages give and do not give: only the Khanate page dates anything territorial, and it does so by reign (Quetta, Mastung and Pishin under Mir Ahmad I 1666-1695; Karachi under Samandar Khan 1697-1714; Bandar Abbas under Abdullah Khan 1716-1731; Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand and Zahedan under Nasir Khan I 1749-1794). The four gains are confidence 1 and dated to the first year of the reign; the researcher's regions are circles round the named towns. Not on any page opened: Makran, Kharan and Las Bela as dated acquisitions, the 1854 treaty, the Quetta lease, Bolan, Nushki, Nasirabad, Chagai, Kachhi as a British lease, the 1896 Iran frontier line, the early-19th-century losses to Iran and Afghanistan (years given only as 'early 19th century'), and the Talpur overlordship (undated, Nasir Khan page). A gap-filler should open 'Treaty of Kalat', 'Siege of Kalat (1839)', 'Quetta', 'Makran' and 'Kharan State'.

Area: infobox 560,000 km2 (1835) and 139,850 km2 (1940). The 1835 figure cannot be reproduced from the named places; it must count the feudatory Makran, Kharan, Las Bela and Persian Baluchistan claims. The grid shape of the 1749 keyframe is about 266,000 km2 (ratio 0.48 to the 1835 claim); the 1941 keyframe resolves to about 142,000 km2 against the infobox's 139,850 km2 for 1940 (ratio 1.02), which supports the three bridged losses (Persian Baluchistan 1828, Karachi 1843, Quetta and Pishin 1877) taken together, not any one of them. Treat the 1835 figure as a claim, not a measurement; the dossier draws no territory the pages do not name, so the 1784-1827 shape still holds all of Nasir Khan's conquests.

Pages disagree: Treaty of Kalat 1875 (lead) or 1876 (body and infobox: 8 December 1876); Treaty of Mastung 1876 or 1877 (Baluchistan Agency page); independence 11 August (infobox) or 12 August 1947 (lead); the Battle of Kachhi 1734 (Khanate page) or 1731 (Nasir Khan page, which has Abdullah Khan die in 1731: the ruler list also has him end 1731).

Counterparts: afsharid-iran (Cliopatria row 1734-1756) stands for Nader Shah; safavid-dynasty for Bandar Abbas; the Agency's Kharan State and Las Bela State, Makran, the Balochistan States Union and Sultan bin Ahmad of Muscat have no dossier (Oman's 18th-century state is not a Cliopatria row: sultanate-of-muscat-and-oman starts 1900). A dossier for Persian Baluchistan or for Kharan and Las Bela would take the 1749 and 1941 events.

Gazetteer names absent: Kalat (Pakistan), Mastung, Pishin, Kharan, Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Las Bela, Kachhi: drawn as coordinate circles (Kalat 66.59 E 29.03 N, Mastung 66.84 29.80, Pishin 66.99 30.58, Kacchi 67.6 28.8, Khash 61.2 28.2, Bampur 60.46 27.2, Qasr-e Qand 60.7 26.24, Kharan 65.4 28.6). The place 'Qalat' in the gazetteer is the Afghan town.

Suzerainty events kept out of the ledger: vassal_start and vassal_end belong in the suzerain's dossier with this state as the counterpart (the schema: 'counterpart is the vassal itself'), so they are listed here for whoever writes or checks the suzerain. 1748 vassal_start (suzerain durrani-empire, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 1748: Kalat a vassal of the Durrani Empire ('From 1748, Kalat was a vassal of the Durrani Empire'). The terms of the later treaty are disputed: 'some sources describe sovereignty, others suzerainty with no tribute'. | 1826 vassal_end (suzerain durrani-empire, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 1826: Afghan influence over Kalat ends 'after the death of Sher Dil Khan of Kandahar in 1826'. The page gives early-19th-century losses of territory to Qajar Iran and to the Emirate of Afghanistan without years; none is drawn. | 1876-12 vassal_start (suzerain british-raj, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 8 December 1876: the Treaty of Kalat with Robert Sandeman. Kalat became 'a self-governing state in a subsidiary alliance, supervised by the Baluchistan Agency' (the lead says 1875, the body and infobox 1876; the Agency page: established 1877 'following the 1876 treaty'). Leases and cessions such as Quetta are not on the pages opened. | 1947-08 vassal_end (suzerain british-raj, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 11 August 1947: the Khan declares independence (the lead says 12 August). | 1948-03 vassal_start (suzerain islamic-republic-of-pakistan, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 27 March 1948: Kalat accedes to Pakistan ('accepted by Jinnah on 31 March') while keeping internal self-government; the Khan's brother led a revolt that the Pakistan Army suppressed. | 1955-10 vassal_end (suzerain islamic-republic-of-pakistan, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanate_of_Kalat): 14 October 1955: incorporated into West Pakistan; the Khan had headed the Balochistan States Union since 3 October 1952.
